extracted.intended_audience: immigration attorneys, petitioners, program sponsors, and USCIS adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements in 8 CFR part 214 governing J-, K-, and L-class nonimmigrants (employment authorization, reporting, petitions, evidence, blanket petitions, approvals/denials, and revocation). Useful for preparing petitions, advising beneficiaries, and adjudicating eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: J-2 employment authorization: application requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for employment authorization must be made on Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization, with fee, as required by the Service, to the district director having jurisdiction over the J-1 exchange visitor's temporary residence in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must use Form I-765 and include the required fee; file with the district director having jurisdiction over the J-1's temporary residence. (Surrounding context notes use and limitations of J-2 employment income.)

rubrics_metrics.name: J-2 employment authorization: allowed duration and maintenance condition
rubrics_metrics.description: J-2 employment may be authorized for the duration of the J-1 principal alien's authorized stay as indicated on Form I-94 or a period of four years, whichever is shorter. The employment authorization is valid only if the J-1 is maintaining status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a J-2 has filed a timely application for extension of stay, renewal of employment authorization on Form I-765 with fee is only possible upon approval of the extension of stay. Employment authorization therefore ties to the J-1's status and approved extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: J-2 income use restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment will not be authorized if this income is needed to support the J-1 principal alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although J-2 income may be used to support family recreational and cultural activities, authorization is withheld if the income is required to support the J-1 principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of J-1 duration of status when H‑1B numerical limit likely reached
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may, by notice in the Federal Register, extend for such a period as necessary to complete adjudication of an H-1B application on behalf of a J-1 alien when the H-1B numerical limitation will likely be reached prior to the end of a fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) employer has timely filed an application for change of status to H-1B on behalf of the J-1; (2) the alien must not have violated terms of nonimmigrant stay and must not be subject to the 2‑year foreign residence requirement at section 212(e) of the Act. Extension also applies to J-2 dependents; an extension under this paragraph causes the J-1 to be considered maintaining lawful nonimmigrant status for all purposes provided the J-1 complies with J nonimmigrant terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS mandatory use for designated program sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: At a date to be established by the Department of State and announced in the Federal Register, the use of the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) will become mandatory for designated program sponsors; all designated program sponsors must begin issuance of the SEVIS Form DS-2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors should monitor Federal Register announcements and begin issuing DS-2019 in SEVIS when the mandatory date is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: J-1 current name and address notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A J-1 exchange visitor must inform the Service and the responsible officer of the exchange visitor program of any legal changes to his or her name or of any change of address, within 10 days of the change, in a manner prescribed by the program sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enrolled in SEVIS, the exchange visitor can satisfy 8 CFR 265.1 by providing notice within 10 days to the responsible officer, who shall enter the information in SEVIS within 21 days. Non-SEVIS program participants must submit change of address to the Service as provided in 8 CFR 265.1 within 10 days. The address must be the actual physical location of residence (not merely a mailing address), and sponsors must keep records of actual physical locations and provide them on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate medical trainees: annual Form I-644 reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exchange alien participating in a program of graduate medical education or training shall file Form I-644 (Supplementary Statement for Graduate Medical Trainees) annually with the Service attesting to the conditions as specified on the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form I-644 must also be submitted as an attachment to a completed Form DS-2019 when applying for an extension of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange visitors in cancelled programs: authorization to remain and transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When approval of an exchange visitor program is withdrawn, participants currently engaged in activities authorized by the cancelled program are authorized to remain in the United States to engage in those activities until expiration of their previously authorized period of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District director must notify participants and the sponsor; participants may obtain permission to remain or extension of stay if accepted into another approved program and a Form DS-2019 executed by the new sponsor is submitted; a release from the sponsor of the cancelled program is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for J-1 classification for graduate medical education/training
rubrics_metrics.description: Any alien coming as an exchange visitor to participate in a program under which the alien will receive graduate medical education or training (or seeking to change status on Form I-506 for that purpose) must have passed parts I and II of the National Board of Medical Examiners Examination (or equivalent as determined by HHS), be competent in oral and written English, and submit a completely executed and valid Form DS-2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation also contains historical/exemption language for a 1978–1983 period, but the operative rule requires NBME exam passage (or equivalent), English competency, and valid DS-2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee remittance for J-1 applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who applies for J-1 nonimmigrant status in order to commence participation in a Department of State-designated exchange visitor program is required to pay the SEVIS fee to DHS, pursuant to 8 CFR 214.13, except as otherwise provided in that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow 8 CFR 214.13 for fee payment and any enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-1/K-2 petition requirement and supporting document rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To be classified as a fiance or fiancee under section 101(a)(15)(K)(i), an alien must be the beneficiary of an approved visa petition filed on Form I-129F. A copy of a supporting document may be accepted without the original if it bears an attorney's certification as provided in § 204.2(j); however, the original shall be submitted if requested by the Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should provide Form I-129F and attach supporting documents; certified copies may be used unless originals are requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-1 in-person meeting requirement and discretionary exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish to the director's satisfaction that the petitioner and K-1 beneficiary have met in person within the two years immediately preceding the filing of the petition. The director may exempt this requirement only for extreme hardship to the petitioner or if meeting would violate long-established customs of the beneficiary's foreign culture/social practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain an exemption, petitioner must show that compliance would result in extreme hardship or violate customs and also establish that other aspects of the traditional arrangements have been/will be met. Failure to meet or obtain a waiver results in denial of the petition (without prejudice to filing a new petition after meeting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative children of K-1 beneficiary
rubrics_metrics.description: Without approval of a separate petition, a child of the beneficiary may be accorded the same nonimmigrant classification as the beneficiary if accompanying or following to join him or her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children defined under section 101(b)(1)(A)–(E) may receive derivative classification when accompanying or following to join the K-1 beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to petitioner on petition decision and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall be notified of the decision and, if the petition is denied, of the reasons therefor and of the right to appeal in accordance with part 103 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial notices must explain grounds and describe appeals procedures under part 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-1 petition validity, revalidation, and termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of a petition under this paragraph shall be valid for a period of four months. A petition which has expired may be revalidated by a director or consular officer for a period of four months upon finding that the petitioner and K-1 beneficiary are free to marry and intend to marry within 90 days of the beneficiary's entry. Approval is automatically terminated when the petitioner dies or files a written withdrawal before beneficiary arrival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should monitor expiration and seek revalidation if necessary; termination events (death, withdrawal) effect immediate termination of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-3/K-4 eligibility: required petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: To be classified as a K-3 spouse or K-4 child, the alien spouse must be the beneficiary of an immigrant visa petition filed by a U.S. citizen on Form I-130 and the beneficiary of an approved petition for a K-3 nonimmigrant visa filed on Form I-129F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both underlying I-130 and approved I-129F for K-3 are required for K-3/K-4 classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of admission for K-3/K-4 status
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens entering the United States as a K-3 shall be admitted for a period of 2 years. K-4 aliens shall be admitted for 2 years or until their 21st birthday, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission periods are defined and are limited; plan filings accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization procedures for K nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien admitted under section 101(a)(15)(K) shall be authorized to work incident to status for the period of authorized stay. K-1/K-2 aliens seeking work authorization must apply, with fee, to the Service for work authorization pursuant to § 274a.12(a)(6). K-3/K-4 aliens must apply for a document evidencing employment authorization pursuant to § 274a.12(a)(9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment authorization documents issued to K-3/K-4 aliens may be renewed only upon a showing that the applicant has an application or petition awaiting approval equivalent to the showing required for an extension of stay pursuant to § 214.2(k)(10).

rubrics_metrics.name: K-3/K-4 extension of stay: timing and required pending filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A K-3/K-4 alien may apply for extension of stay on Form I-539 120 days prior to expiration. Extensions for K-4 must be filed concurrently with K-3's extension. Extension will be granted in 2‑year intervals upon a showing that one of the specified filings is awaiting approval (e.g., Form I-130 filed by the K-3's U.S. citizen spouse who filed I-129F; application for an immigrant visa based on that I-130; a Form I-485 based on that I-130).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants wishing to extend must show one of the listed petitions/applications is pending with the Service or Department of State as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-3/K-4 good cause standard for extension after I-130 approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens may file for extension of stay as a K-3/K-4 after a Form I-130 filed on their behalf has been approved, without filing adjustment of status or immigrant visa, upon a showing of 'good cause' (illness, job loss, or other catastrophic event that prevented filing adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The events must have occurred since entry as K-3/K-4; burden of proof rests solely with applicant; the decision is purely discretionary and not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of K-3/K-4 status events and 30-day rule
rubrics_metrics.description: K-3/K-4 status shall be automatically terminated 30 days following occurrence of any of the listed events: denial or revocation of the Form I-130 filed on behalf of that alien; denial/revocation of the immigrant visa application; denial/revocation of the adjustment of status application; divorce of the K-3 spouse from the U.S. citizen; marriage of an alien in K-4 status; denial of petitions/applications to K-3 also results in termination of dependent K-4's status. For purposes of this section, there is no denial or revocation until administrative appeal is exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the 30‑day automatic termination window and interplay with administrative appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intracompany transferee (L) general admission criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An intracompany transferee is an alien who within the three years preceding application has been employed abroad continuously for one year by a qualifying organization and seeks to enter the U.S. temporarily to render services to a parent, branch, affiliate, or subsidiary in a managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge capacity. Periods in U.S. lawful status for the same employer and brief business or pleasure trips do not interrupt the one year but do not count toward it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the alien's prior employment and the qualifying relationship of employers must be demonstrated; the U.S. employer/petitioner and the alien must meet definitions set out in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial capacity definition for L classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Managerial capacity means an assignment in which the employee primarily: (1) manages the organization or a department/subdivision/function; (2) supervises and controls the work of supervisory/professional/managerial employees or manages an essential function; (3) has authority to hire and fire or recommend personnel actions (or, if no direct supervisees, functions at a senior level); and (4) exercises discretion over day-to-day operations. A first-line supervisor is not managerial merely by supervisory duties unless the employees supervised are professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four prongs to evaluate whether position is managerial; mere supervision of non-professional staff generally insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive capacity definition for L classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive capacity means an assignment in which the employee primarily: (1) directs management of the organization or a major component/function; (2) establishes goals and policies; (3) exercises wide latitude in discretionary decision-making; and (4) receives only general supervision from higher executives, board, or stockholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive roles require high-level decision-making authority and autonomy; adjudicators should assess these factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized knowledge and specialized knowledge professional definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized knowledge means special knowledge possessed by an individual of the petitioning organization's product, service, research, equipment, techniques, management, or other interests and its application in international markets, or an advanced level of knowledge or expertise in the organization's processes and procedures. A specialized knowledge professional is an individual who has such specialized knowledge and is a member of the professions as defined in section 101(a)(32) of the INA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that knowledge is specific to the petitioning organization and not generally available; for 'professional' classification also demonstrate membership in the professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: New office and qualifying organization definitions and doing-business standard
rubrics_metrics.description: New office means an organization doing business in the U.S. through a parent/branch/affiliate/subsidiary for less than one year. Qualifying organization means a U.S. or foreign firm meeting a qualifying relationship, doing business in the U.S. and at least one other country for the duration of the alien's stay, and otherwise meeting INA requirements. Doing business means the regular, systematic, and continuous provision of goods/services and does not include mere presence of an agent or office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicators review corporate relationships, continuity of business, and whether operations are regular/systematic/continuous rather than token presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of petitions: disclosure and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner seeking L classification must file a petition on the form prescribed by USCIS, advise whether a previous petition for the same beneficiary has been filed, and certify that another petition will not be filed unless circumstances change. Failure to make full disclosure of previous petitions may result in denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and candid disclosure is required; special blanket petition rules are provided separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required with individual L petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual petition must be accompanied by: (i) evidence that the petitioner and the employing organization are qualifying organizations; (ii) evidence the alien will be employed in an executive/managerial/specialized knowledge capacity including detailed job description; (iii) evidence the alien has at least one continuous year of full-time employment abroad with a qualifying organization within the three years preceding filing; (iv) evidence that prior employment abroad was managerial, executive, or specialized and that prior education/training/employment qualifies the alien for the intended U.S. services; (v) if opening a new office as manager/executive, evidence of premises, prior year employment in executive/managerial capacity, and that the U.S. operation will support such a position within one year with supporting information on nature/structure/finances; (vi) if specialized-knowledge opening new office, evidence of premises, qualifying organization status in U.S., and financial ability to remunerate and commence business; (vii) if beneficiary is owner/major stockholder, evidence services are temporary and that beneficiary will be transferred abroad upon completion; (viii) such other evidence as director may deem necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an inclusive list; new office cases have special documentary thresholds (premises, financials, business plan/organizational structure). Adjudicators have discretion to request additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blanket petition eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner meeting the following may file a blanket petition: (A) engaged in commercial trade or services; (B) has a U.S. office that has been doing business for one year or more; (C) has three or more domestic and foreign branches, subsidiaries, or affiliates; and (D) has obtained approval of petitions for at least ten L managers/executives/specialized professionals in the prior 12 months; or has U.S. subsidiaries/affiliates with combined annual sales of at least $25 million; or has a U.S. workforce of at least 1,000 employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfy one of the alternative size/experience criteria in (D) in addition to (A)-(C) to qualify for blanket petition filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blanket petition procedures: certification, Form I-129S, and consular/Service determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: For blanket petitions: qualifying organization completes Form I-129S (Certificate of Eligibility for Intracompany Transferee under a Blanket Petition) in original and copies; employee may use Form I-797 plus I-129S to apply for visa issuance within six months; consular or Service officer determines whether the U.S. position is with an organization named in the approved petition and whether the job is managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge and whether the alien's prior year abroad was with an organization named and in an appropriate position. Consular officers may grant L classification only in clearly approvable applications and may issue 'Blanket L-1'/'Blanket L-2' visas and stamp/endorse Form I-129S with validity up to three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For visa-exempt nonimmigrants and in‑U.S. change-of-status under blanket petitions, the petitioner files I-129S with the USCIS office where blanket was filed. When admissible under blanket petition, an alien may be reassigned among listed organizations without Service referral if performing virtually the same job duties; otherwise a new Certificate of Eligibility is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting document copies rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner may submit a legible photocopy of a document in support of the visa petition in lieu of the original document. However, the original shall be submitted if requested by the Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep originals available for production upon Service request; provide legible photocopies with petitions to reduce risk of losing originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval processing time, Form I-797 content, validity periods, and amendment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The director shall notify the petitioner of approval within 30 days after the date a completed petition has been filed; if additional information is required the 30‑day period begins again upon receipt. Form I-797 for individual petition shall include beneficiary's name, classification and petition's validity. Individual petitions are valid for period of established need not to exceed three years (one year limit for new office cases unless extended). Blanket petitions initially valid for three years and may be extended indefinitely if complying. The petitioner must file an amended petition with fee to reflect changes in approved relationships, additional qualifying organizations under a blanket petition, change in capacity of employment (e.g., specialized knowledge to managerial), or any information affecting eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicators restart the 30‑day clock when requests for additional info made; petitioners must seek amendments when material changes occur to avoid invalid approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spouse and dependent L classification and employment restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The spouse and unmarried minor children of the beneficiary are entitled to L nonimmigrant classification, subject to the same period of admission and limits as the beneficiary, if accompanying or following to join. Neither spouse nor child may accept employment unless granted employment authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependents receive derivative L status but must obtain separate employment authorization before working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of petitions: notice, reasons, and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual or blanket petition is denied the petitioner shall be notified within 30 days after filing of the denial, the reasons for the denial, and the right to appeal. If a blanket petition is denied in part, the USCIS office shall forward Form I-797 listing organizations found to qualify. If denial is reversed on appeal, a new Form I-797 will be sent to reflect changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial notices must state reasons and inform of appeal rights; partial blanket denials require identification of qualifying organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of individual and blanket petition approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: The director may revoke a petition at any time, even after expiration. Approval is automatically revoked if the petitioner withdraws the petition or fails to request indefinite validity of a blanket petition. The director shall send a notice of intent to revoke if he/she finds among other grounds: one or more entities are no longer qualifying organizations; the alien is no longer eligible; a qualifying organization violated requirements; the statement of facts was not true and correct; approval involved gross error; or none of the qualifying organizations have used the blanket petition procedure for three consecutive years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of intent to revoke must contain detailed grounds and time period allowed for rebuttal (30 days). Upon receipt, petitioner may submit rebuttal evidence within 30 days which the director will consider in deciding whether to revoke in whole or part.
